## Goal
When you finish, `apps/mobile` is an Expo SDK 57 / React Native 0.86 application using expo-router, named `mobile` in the workspace, that boots to a placeholder screen, exports cleanly for Android and passes `expo-doctor`. It carries the whole project configuration the later mobile steps build on: `app.config.ts` (Anacast identity, env-driven `googleServicesFile` and EAS project id, plugins), `eas.json` (three build profiles), monorepo Metro config, Babel, TypeScript and ESLint wiring, the theme token file, the Supabase client built from `@church/supabase-client`'s `createMobileClient` with the Expo adapters injected, the TanStack Query client persisted through `expo-sqlite/kv-store`, and a root layout with all providers. Every route file of PLAN §9 exists as a typed placeholder so `expo-router`'s typed routes compile; the real screens arrive in 4.1b (auth, org gate), 4.2a/4.2b (feed, sermons) and 4.3 (push, More tab, notification settings). Nothing here needs a hosted Supabase project or an Expo account; the founder's EAS/Firebase work is step 4.5.

## Goal
When you finish, the Expo app from 4.1a has a complete sign-in flow and a tenancy gate. A person opens the app, enters the email their church has on file, receives a 6-digit code (the founder edits the Supabase Magic Link template to include `{{ .Token }}` in step 2.4 — DESIGN §5: "otherwise `signInWithOtp` sends a link"), types the code and lands in the tabs of their church. A tap on an invitation deep link `anacast://invite/<token>` (from the web invite page's "Open in app" button built in 2.1b) carries the token through sign-in and accepts the invitation with `accept_invitation`. Users with an account but no active membership see the `no-church` screen. Members of several churches get a switcher; the choice persists locally and in `profiles.last_org_id`. No feed, no players, no push yet (4.2a, 4.2b, 4.3).

## Inputs / prior state

Scheme `anacast` is configured in `app.config.ts` and asserted equal to `APP_SCHEME`.

Read `packages/db/src/rpc.ts` and `queries/*.ts` for exact names before importing — do not invent parallel helpers.
- `9999_init.sql` (1.3b): `accept_invitation(token)` verifies hash/expiry, requires the caller's `profiles.email` to equal the invitation email (`invitation_email_mismatch`), requires the org writable (`organization_suspended`), upserts the membership as `active`, creates a one-person household when no person is linked, merges for an existing member. `my_context()` returns memberships in every status except `disabled`; `membership_status` may be `pending` (Phase 2 join requests) — only `active` counts as access.

## Build
1. **Session provider** `src/features/auth/SessionProvider.tsx`: on mount `supabase.auth.getSession()`, then `onAuthStateChange((event, session) => …)`; expose `useSession()` → `{ session, userId, status: 'loading' | 'signed_out' | 'signed_in' }`. On `SIGNED_OUT` clear `active_org_id` from kv and call `queryClient.clear()` (the persisted cache must not leak one account's feed to the next). Mount it inside `app/_layout.tsx` under `AppQueryProvider`. Keep the splash screen up until `status !== 'loading'`.
2. **Context query** `src/features/auth/useMyContext.ts`: `useQuery({ queryKey: queryKeys.context(), queryFn: () => myContext(supabase), enabled: status === 'signed_in', staleTime: 60_000 })`; export `activeOrgs(ctx)` = orgs with `membership_status === 'active'` (pure, tested); `refreshContext()` = `invalidateQueries(queryKeys.context())`.
3. **`(auth)/sign-in`** (`app/(auth)/sign-in.tsx`, `src/features/auth/SignInForm.tsx`, react-native-paper inputs, `react-hook-form` is NOT used on mobile — keep plain controlled inputs validated with the Zod schemas): title "Sign in to Anacast"; email field; primary button "Email me a code" → validate with `otpRequestSchema` → `supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({ email, options: { shouldCreateUser: <see rule> } })` → on success `router.push({ pathname: '/(auth)/verify-otp', params: { email } })`. Ask your church for an invitation." Secondary link "Use a password instead" reveals a password field and swaps the button to "Sign in" → `emailPasswordSchema` → `signInWithPassword`; wrong credentials → "Email or password is incorrect" (never leak which). Link "Forgot password?" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(`${publicEnv().webUrl}/auth/reset`)` (password reset stays on the web, DESIGN §5). Footer: "By signing in you agree to the Terms and Privacy Policy" linking to `${webUrl}/terms` and `${webUrl}/privacy`. Disable buttons while pending; show `DomainError`/auth messages inline, never raw error objects. Rate-limit friendliness: after a successful send, disable "Email me a code" for 60 s (Supabase default OTP throttle) and say so.
4. **`(auth)/verify-otp`** (`app/(auth)/verify-otp.tsx`, `src/features/auth/OtpForm.tsx`): reads `email` from `useLocalSearchParams`; a single 6-digit numeric field (`keyboardType: 'number-pad'`, `autoComplete: 'one-time-code'`, `textContentType: 'oneTimeCode'`); auto-submits at 6 digits → `otpVerifySchema` → `supabase.auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email' })`; on success the session provider fires and `app/index.tsx` routes on; expired/invalid → "That code is wrong or has expired" with a "Send a new code" button (60 s cooldown, same `signInWithOtp` call). 5. **`(auth)/invite/[token]`** (`app/(auth)/invite/[token].tsx`, `src/features/auth/useAcceptInvitation.ts`): reached by `anacast://invite/<token>` (expo-router maps the scheme URL to this route automatically; verify with `npx uri-scheme open "anacast://invite/abc" --android` in the docs, and with a unit test of the pure parser below). Validate with `invitationTokenSchema`; malformed → friendly "This invitation link is not valid" + "Go to sign in" (never crash). Signed out → `setKv('pending_invite_token', token)` and `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')` with an inline notice "Sign in with the email address the invitation was sent to". Signed in → call `acceptInvitation(supabase, { token })`: success → `deleteKv('pending_invite_token')`, `refreshContext()`, set active org to the returned `org_id` (Build 7's `switchOrg`), `router.replace('/(app)/(tabs)/home')`, toast "Welcome to <org name>"; `invitation_email_mismatch` → explain that the signed-in email differs, offer "Sign out and try again"; `invitation_expired`/`invitation_invalid` → message from `DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES` + "Ask your church for a new invitation"; `organization_suspended` → its message. The same hook runs once from `app/index.tsx` when a session appears and `pending_invite_token` exists (the post-sign-in resume path).
6. **`(auth)/no-church`** (`app/(auth)/no-church.tsx`): "You are signed in as <email>. Your account is not linked to a church yet. Ask your church to invite you or to create your account." (DESIGN §10 wording), buttons "Check again" (`refreshContext()`), "Sign out". If any org has `membership_status === 'pending'`, add "Your request to join <name> is waiting for approval" (Phase 2 join requests, 5.6, will add join-code entry here — leave a `TODO(5.6)` comment, no UI).
7. **Active organization** `src/features/org/ActiveOrgProvider.tsx` + `useActiveOrg()`: input = `activeOrgs(ctx)`; resolution order: kv `active_org_id` if still active → `ctx.profile.last_org_id` if active → first active org (sorted by name). The provider is mounted in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` only.
8. **Gate** `app/(app)/_layout.tsx`: `useSession()` + `useMyContext()`; while loading → `LoadingState`; signed out → `<Redirect href="/(auth)/sign-in" />`; no active org → `<Redirect href="/(auth)/no-church" />`; otherwise `ActiveOrgProvider` → `<Stack>` with `(tabs)` and the stack screens (`sermons/[id]`, `announcements/[id]`, `bulletins/index`, `bulletins/[id]`, `settings/notifications`) with headers titled by the org name where sensible. Use expo-router `Stack.Protected` guards if the installed `expo-router` exposes them (SDK 53+); otherwise the `Redirect` pattern above. `app/index.tsx`: the session gate — loading → splash; signed out → `/(auth)/sign-in`; signed in + pending invite → run Build 5's resume; signed in → `/(app)/(tabs)/home`. `app/(auth)/_layout.tsx`: a `Stack` with a plain header; if a signed-in user with an active org lands on an auth screen (except `invite/[token]`), redirect to home.

10. **Sign-out helper** `src/features/auth/signOut.ts`: `signOutEverywhere()` → placeholder call `await beforeSignOut()` (4.3 registers push-device deletion here — export a `registerBeforeSignOut(fn)` hook so 4.3 does not edit this file's logic), `supabase.auth.signOut()`, kv cleanup (`active_org_id`, `pending_invite_token`), `queryClient.clear()`, `router.replace('/(auth)/sign-in')`. Used by `no-church` now and by More/sign-out in 4.3.
11. **Deep-link parsing (pure, tested)** `src/lib/links.ts`: `parseAppLink(url)` → `{ kind: 'invite', token } | { kind: 'unknown' }` for `anacast://invite/<token>` and `https://<any host>/invite/<token>` (App Links arrive in 5.7 — the parser is ready now), using `invitationTokenSchema`; used by an `Linking.useURL()` effect in `app/_layout.tsx` only for the https form (expo-router already routes the scheme form). `src/lib/links.test.ts` covers both forms, a malformed token, and an unrelated URL.

No component tests (no jsdom for RN in this step).

## Goal
When you finish, the Sermons tab lists the active church's published sermons and a sermon page plays them. The player has exactly four strategies, chosen by the shared parser and the sermon's `media_kind`: (1) `expo-audio` for uploaded audio and audio streams — plays in the background with lock-screen/notification controls; (2) `expo-video` for uploaded video and video streams — fullscreen and picture-in-picture; (3) `react-native-webview` loading OUR hosted page `/embed/yt/[id]` (built on the web in 3.4b) for YouTube, because YouTube's embed player needs a valid referer that a bare WebView cannot supply (PLAN §1 item 5), with an "Open in YouTube" button; (4) `expo-web-browser` for Google Drive and any link the parser marks `open_external`. Uploaded media never leaves Supabase Storage: the app mints a signed URL with 4.2a's hook and re-mints once when the URL expires or the server answers 403. 6. **`players/Video.tsx`** (`expo-video`): `const player = useVideoPlayer({ uri }, p => { p.staysActiveInBackground = true; p.showNowPlayingNotification = true })`; `<VideoView player={player} nativeControls allowsFullscreen allowsPictureInPicture contentFit="contain" style={{ aspectRatio: 16/9 }} />`; `useEvent(player, 'statusChange')` to surface errors to `SignedMedia`. Add `startsPictureInPictureAutomatically` only if the installed typings have it.
7. **`players/YouTubeWebView.tsx`**: `<WebView source={{ uri: hostedEmbedUrl }} allowsInlineMediaPlayback mediaPlaybackRequiresUserAction={false} javaScriptEnabled domStorageEnabled allowsFullscreenVideo originWhitelist={[webOrigin, 'https://www.youtube-nocookie.com', 'https://www.youtube.com']} onShouldStartLoadWithRequest={(req) => req.url.startsWith(webOrigin) || req.url.includes('youtube')} style={{ aspectRatio: 16/9 }} />` where `hostedEmbedUrl` is built with the `@church/domain` builder + `publicEnv().webUrl` (this page supplies the referer YouTube requires — PLAN §1 item 5; do NOT load `youtube.com/embed` directly and do NOT add `react-native-youtube-iframe`, DESIGN §3); below it a button "Open in YouTube" → `WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync(canonicalUrl)`; helper text "Unlisted videos work; private videos and videos with embedding disabled do not" (DESIGN §7). No background audio for YouTube (ToS) — say so in a one-line caption when the app is backgrounded? No: just do not request it.

11. **Tests**: `playerStrategy.test.ts` (table above), `formatDuration.test.ts` (`mm:ss`, `h:mm:ss`), `hostedEmbedUrl.test.ts` (joins `webUrl` and the domain builder without double slashes). Mock Expo modules with `vi.mock`.

## Constraints

- Never `expo-av`, never `react-native-youtube-iframe`, never load `youtube.com/embed` straight into the WebView (DESIGN §3, §7). No media proxying through the web app; no downloading of sermon files (Phase 4).
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install`; if you truly need a slider package, install it that way and record it in HANDOFF version pins.
- Signed URL constants and hook from 4.2a only; `meta: { persist: false }` stays; never log signed URLs.
- Do not build push, the More tab, notification settings (4.3), share links or uploads (web). Do not touch `apps/web`, migrations (never `supabase db push`), shared packages except additive exports you record.
- No secrets; no model identifiers in commits or files.

- `cd apps/mobile && npx expo-doctor` → no issues; with the 4.1a mock env `npx expo export --platform android --output-dir dist` → succeeds (`rm -rf dist`).

- `npx expo config --type public` (mock env) → `plugins` still include `expo-audio` with `enableBackgroundPlayback: true` and `expo-video` with `supportsBackgroundPlayback: true`.
- Static review: navigating from one sermon to another disposes the previous player; `SignedMedia` re-mints at most once per failure cycle; the YouTube WebView `source.uri` starts with `publicEnv().webUrl`.
- With a development build after 4.5: play an uploaded mp3, lock the phone — audio continues and the notification shows the title; play a YouTube-linked sermon — the hosted page loads and plays inline; a Drive link opens the browser. Record in HANDOFF whether this was possible in this session.

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: State — "Mobile: sermons + playback (4.2b)"; feature table — Sermons Mobile UI `done (4.2b)` (playback only; upload/link/delete/share remain web); "Decisions" — the four strategies and the referer rationale, one player at a time, no offline downloads; "Version pins" — any package added via `expo install` (slider); "Deviations from plan" — lock-screen API availability, anything else; founder to-dos — none new (device checks happen in 4.5).

steps.title: Push & deep links
steps.goal: The app registers for push and reacts to it: after the first sign-in an explainer asks permission, the Android channel `announcements` (importance high) is created, `requestPermissionsAsync` runs (POST_NOTIFICATIONS on Android 13+), `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` obtains the Expo token and the device is upserted into `push_devices` (deleted again on sign-out); a notification tap or cold start with a notification response reads `data.url` + `data.org_id` written by the web dispatcher (3.6a), switches the active org when needed and routes to `/announcements/<id>` or `/bulletins/<id>`; `settings/notifications` edits the per-church `notification_preferences` (announcements, bulletins) and shows device/permission status; the More tab gets its real rows (Bulletins, Notification settings, Switch church, Sign out, privacy/terms, version). Registration is skipped gracefully on emulators and in Expo Go, errors never block the app, and the pure pieces are unit-tested.
steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 4.3 "Push & deep links" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §1 item 6, §7 (Push row), §9 (Push bullet) and `docs/DESIGN.md` §4 (Notifications & devices), §6 (`push_devices`/`notification_preferences` policies), §8 (Push fan-out row), §10 (Push bullet), §13 risk 5 before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one.

## Goal
When you finish, a member who signs in on a real Android device built with EAS (step 4.5) is asked once whether Anacast may notify them; if they agree, the device appears in `public.push_devices` and, when a leader publishes an announcement or uploads a bulletin on the web, the dispatcher from 3.6a sends a push that lands on the phone; tapping it opens the right announcement or bulletin in the right church, even from a cold start. Members control which kinds they receive per church on `settings/notifications`, and signing out removes the device row so a shared phone never keeps receiving another person's church news. The More tab becomes the real menu (Bulletins, Notification settings, Switch church, Sign out, Privacy / Terms links, app version). DESIGN §10: "Android push requires the dev client / EAS build (not Expo Go)" — the code must detect and explain that, never crash.

## Inputs / prior state
- 4.1a–4.2b produced: `supabase`, `useSession()`, `useActiveOrg()` (`{ org, orgs, switchOrg(orgId), … }`), `useOrgSwitcher()`, `signOutEverywhere()` + `registerBeforeSignOut(fn)`, `src/lib/kv.ts` (keys `push_token`, `push_explainer_seen`), `publicEnv().webUrl`, the tabs, `bulletins/index`, `bulletins/[id]`, `announcements/[id]` (cold-start safe), placeholders `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` and `app/(app)/settings/notifications.tsx`. 4.1a installed `expo-notifications`, `expo-device`, `expo-constants` and configured the `expo-notifications` plugin (icon, colour) and `extra.eas.projectId: process.env.EAS_PROJECT_ID` in `app.config.ts`.
- Schema (1.2, read `packages/db/src/database.types.ts`): `push_devices (id, user_id fk auth.users cascade, expo_push_token text not null unique, platform push_platform ('android' | 'ios') not null, device_name text, enabled boolean default true, last_seen_at, created_at, updated_at)`; `notification_preferences (user_id, org_id, announcements bool default true, bulletins bool default true, events bool default true, surveys bool default true, updated_at)` PK `(user_id, org_id)`. Policies (DESIGN §6): both tables `user_id = auth.uid()` for all ops — the app writes its own rows directly through the query helpers; `remove_membership` deletes the user's `push_devices`/`notification_preferences` for that org server-side.
- `@church/db` (1.7a, `queries/notifications.ts`): `upsertPushDevice(db, userId, { expo_push_token, platform, device_name })` on the token unique key, `deletePushDevice(db, token)`, `disablePushDevice(db, token)`, `getNotificationPreferences(db, userId, orgId)`, `upsertNotificationPreferences(db, …)`; `queryKeys.notifications.*` or `.preferences(…)` — read `keys.ts`; add additively (with a test) if a key is missing.
- `@church/domain` (1.6b): `schemas/notifications.ts` — `registerPushDeviceSchema` (`expo_push_token` matching `^Expo(nent)?PushToken\[.+\]$`, `platform`, `device_name` optional) and `notificationPreferencesSchema` (`org_id`, `announcements`, `bulletins`, `events`, `surveys`); `urls.ts` — `notificationTargetPath(kind, refId)` → `/announcements/<id>`, `/bulletins/<id>`, `/events/<id>`, `/surveys/<id>` (3.6a: "the app-relative route the mobile app (4.3) pushes after switching to `org_id`").
- Web 3.6a dispatcher message shape (fixed — read `apps/web/src/lib/push/dispatch.ts`): `{ to: expo_push_token, title, body (≤ 178 chars), data: { url: notificationTargetPath(kind, refId), org_id, kind, ref_id, notification_id }, sound: 'default', channelId: 'announcements', priority: 'high' }`; recipients = `srv_audience_user_ids` ∩ `notification_preferences` for the kind ∩ `push_devices.enabled`; 3.6a/3.6b receipts mark `DeviceNotRegistered` tokens `enabled = false`. Founder decision 6: bulletins push by default (`push_on_bulletin`), so `kind` may be `bulletin`.
- Founder decision 9 / orchestrator decision 5: scheme `anacast`; the founder's `EAS_PROJECT_ID` arrives in step 4.5 — the app must behave when it is undefined (dev builds before `eas init`).

## Build
1. **Notification handler & channel** `src/lib/push.ts`: at module load `Notifications.setNotificationHandler({ handleNotification: async () => ({ shouldShowBanner: true, shouldShowList: true, shouldPlaySound: true, shouldSetBadge: false }) })` (use the property names the installed `expo-notifications` typings expose — `shouldShowAlert` on older ones). `ensureAndroidChannel()`: `Platform.OS === 'android'` → `setNotificationChannelAsync('announcements', { name: 'Announcements', importance: AndroidImportance.HIGH, sound: 'default', vibrationPattern: [0, 250, 250, 250] })` — the id must equal the dispatcher's `channelId: 'announcements'`.
2. **Capability check (pure, tested)** `src/lib/push/capability.ts`: `pushCapability({ isDevice, appOwnership, executionEnvironment, projectId })` → `'ok' | 'emulator' | 'expo_go' | 'missing_project_id'` from `Device.isDevice`, `Constants.appOwnership === 'expo'` / `Constants.executionEnvironment === 'storeClient'`, and `projectId = Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId ?? Constants.easConfig?.projectId` (DESIGN §10). Messages: emulator → "Push notifications need a physical device"; expo_go → "Push needs the Anacast app build (not Expo Go)"; missing_project_id → "This build has no EAS project id — see docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md" (developer-facing, shown only in dev builds; in production log it and stay silent).
3. **Registration** `registerForPush({ userId })` in `src/lib/push.ts`: capability check → `ensureAndroidChannel()` → `getPermissionsAsync()`; if `undetermined` (or `canAskAgain`) → `requestPermissionsAsync()` (this is the Android 13+ POST_NOTIFICATIONS prompt); `denied` → return `{ status: 'denied' }`; `granted` → `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` → validate `{ expo_push_token: token.data, platform: Platform.OS, device_name: Device.modelName ?? undefined }` with `registerPushDeviceSchema` → `upsertPushDevice(supabase, userId, row)` → `setKv('push_token', token.data)` → return `{ status: 'registered', token }`. Errors (network, RLS, invalid token) → `{ status: 'error', message }` — never throw into the UI tree. `refreshPushDevice()`: on every app foreground with a stored token and a session, re-upsert (sets `last_seen_at`, re-enables a device that receipts disabled after the user reinstalled) — throttle to once per 24 h via a kv timestamp `push_last_seen_sync`.
4. **Explainer** `app/(app)/push-explainer.tsx` (modal presentation in the `(app)` stack) + `src/features/push/usePushOnboarding.ts`: after the org gate passes and `push_explainer_seen` is unset and capability is `ok`, present once: "Get notified when <org name> posts an announcement or a bulletin" with "Turn on notifications" (→ `registerForPush`; on `denied` show how to enable in system settings via `Linking.openSettings()`) and "Not now" — both set `push_explainer_seen = 'true'`. Never show it in Expo Go or on emulators (capability ≠ ok → mark seen and skip). If permission is already granted (reinstall), register silently without the modal.
5. **Sign-out cleanup**: in `src/features/push/index.ts` call `registerBeforeSignOut(async () => { const token = await getKv('push_token'); if (token) { await deletePushDevice(supabase, token).catch(noop); await deleteKv('push_token'); } })` — the delete runs BEFORE `auth.signOut()` (RLS `user_id = auth.uid()` needs the session). Also `Notifications.dismissAllNotificationsAsync()` on sign-out.
6. **Deep-link resolution (pure, tested)** `src/lib/deep-links.ts` (file name from DESIGN §11 step 10): `resolveNotificationTarget(data: unknown, ctx: { activeOrgId, orgIds })` → `{ kind: 'navigate', orgId, path } | { kind: 'ignore', reason }`: accept only `data.url` matching `^/(announcements|bulletins|events|surveys)/[0-9a-f-]{36}$` (the four shapes of `notificationTargetPath`) and `data.org_id` a uuid the user actively belongs to (`orgIds`); `events`/`surveys` → for now `ignore` with reason `not_built` (5.3 / 6.1 lift this); anything else → `ignore` (`bad_payload`, `not_member`). Never navigate on attacker-controlled arbitrary URLs.
7. **Response handling** `src/features/push/useNotificationNavigation.ts`, mounted once in `app/(app)/_layout.tsx` after the org gate: (a) `Notifications.addNotificationResponseReceivedListener` (warm taps); (b) cold start — `Notifications.getLastNotificationResponseAsync()` (or the `useLastNotificationResponse` hook) once per app launch, deduplicated by `notification.request.identifier` stored in memory; for each → `resolveNotificationTarget(response.notification.request.content.data, …)`; on `navigate`: if `orgId !== activeOrgId` → `await switchOrg(orgId)`; then `router.push(path)` (expo-router maps `/announcements/<id>` to `app/(app)/announcements/[id].tsx`). Foreground receipt (`addNotificationReceivedListener`): invalidate the feed and bulletins queries so Home refreshes; no in-app banner beyond the system one.
8. **Notification settings** `app/(app)/settings/notifications.tsx` + `src/features/push/NotificationSettings.tsx`: section "This device" — permission status (`granted` / `denied` with "Open system settings" → `Linking.openSettings()`), registration status from kv (`Registered` / `Not registered` + "Register again" → `registerForPush`), the capability message when not `ok`; section "<org name>" — switches for **Announcements** and **Bulletins** bound to `notification_preferences` via `getNotificationPreferences(supabase, userId, orgId)` (treat a missing row as all-true defaults, matching the column defaults) and `upsertNotificationPreferences` validated by `notificationPreferencesSchema` (send all four booleans; keep `events`/`surveys` at their current/default values and do NOT show their switches until 5.3/6.1 — comment `TODO(5.3)`, `TODO(6.1)`); optimistic update with rollback + toast on error; note "Preferences are per church; switch church to change another one". Explain that turning everything off keeps the device registered (the server intersects preferences — DESIGN §8).
9. **More tab** `app/(app)/(tabs)/more.tsx` + `src/features/more/MoreMenu.tsx`: rows Bulletins → `/bulletins`, Notification settings → `/settings/notifications`, Switch church (only when `orgs.length > 1`, opens `useOrgSwitcher().open()`), Sign out (confirm dialog → `signOutEverywhere()`), a footer with "Anacast", `Application.nativeApplicationVersion`/`Constants.expoConfig?.version`, and links Privacy Policy → `${webUrl}/privacy`, Terms → `${webUrl}/terms` (`WebBrowser.openBrowserAsync`); header shows the signed-in email (`useMyContext().profile.email`) and org name. Leave `TODO(5.x)` comments where Directory, Calendar, Documents, My household, Surveys and Delete account rows will go (DESIGN §10).
10. **Tests** (Vitest, node, `vi.mock` for `expo-notifications`, `expo-device`, `expo-constants`): `pushCapability` (four outcomes), `resolveNotificationTarget` (valid announcement, valid bulletin, event → `not_built`, foreign org → `not_member`, external URL → `bad_payload`, missing data), `registerForPush` state machine with mocked permissions (`undetermined → granted → upsert called with a schema-valid row and kv set`, `denied → no upsert`, `getExpoPushTokenAsync` throwing → `error`), the sign-out hook deletes the device before `signOut`.
11. **Docs**: `apps/mobile/README.md` — a "Push" section: what is needed at build time (`google-services.json`, FCM v1 key in EAS — DESIGN §13 risk 5), why Expo Go cannot receive pushes, how to test with `npx expo start --dev-client`, and how to send a test push to a token from the Expo push tool (developer aid). `docs/MOBILE_BUILD.md` is 4.4's.

## Constraints
- All writes through `@church/db` helpers with the user client (RLS `user_id = auth.uid()`); never `supabase.from('push_devices')` in screens; never a service key; never call `srv_*`.
- Payload trust: only `data.url` shapes produced by `notificationTargetPath` and only orgs the user is an active member of; no `Linking.openURL(data.url)`.
- Channel id `announcements`, `projectId` from `Constants.expoConfig.extra.eas.projectId`, token via `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId })` — exactly as DESIGN §10; never `getDevicePushTokenAsync` for the server.
- Native dependency versions only via `npx expo install` (nothing new should be needed; `expo-application` is bundled with `expo` if you want the native version — otherwise use `Constants.expoConfig.version`).
- Do not build directory, events, surveys, join codes, account deletion (later phases). Do not touch `apps/web` (the dispatcher contract is fixed by 3.6a), migrations (never `supabase db push`), or shared packages except additive query keys you record.
- No secrets, no real tokens in tests (use `ExponentPushToken[test-token]`), no model identifiers.

## Verify
- `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` → green; `pnpm --filter mobile test` shows `capability`, `deep-links`, `registerForPush`, `signOutHook` tests passing.
- `cd apps/mobile && npx expo-doctor` → no issues; with the 4.1a mock env `npx expo export --platform android --output-dir dist` → succeeds (`rm -rf dist`).
- `git grep -n "'announcements'" apps/mobile/src/lib/push.ts` → the channel id; `git grep -n "getDevicePushTokenAsync\|openURL(data" apps/mobile` → nothing; `git grep -n "supabase.from(" apps/mobile/src apps/mobile/app` → nothing.
- Static review: the device delete runs before `auth.signOut()`; `resolveNotificationTarget` rejects `https://…` in `data.url`; the explainer never appears when capability ≠ ok; `push_devices` upsert row validates against `registerPushDeviceSchema`.
- With a preview/dev build on a physical Android phone and the hosted project (step 4.5 — Checkpoint C): accept the explainer → SQL Editor `select platform, enabled, device_name from public.push_devices` shows the phone; publish an announcement on the web with push on → the notification arrives within seconds; tap it with the app killed → the announcement opens; sign out → the row is gone. Record in HANDOFF whether this was possible in this session (normally it is verified by the founder in 4.5).

## Finish
- `HANDOFF.md`: State — "Mobile: push registration, deep links, notification settings, More tab (4.3)"; feature table — "Announcements + push" Mobile UI `done (4.3)`, Bulletins push `done`; "Decisions" — channel id, payload validation rule, per-24 h `last_seen_at` refresh, events/surveys switches hidden until 5.3/6.1; "Deviations from plan" — anything that differed; founder to-dos — 4.5 must upload the FCM v1 key and set `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` + `EAS_PROJECT_ID` before the first build, and the founder's own account must be an active member with a device to receive the Checkpoint C push.
- Tick step 4.3 in `docs/TODO.md`; write `session_log.md`; commit `feat(mobile): push registration, notification deep links, notification settings, More tab`; push (`git push origin main` unless another branch was named). If something in the plan proves impossible or wrong, do the closest correct thing, record it in HANDOFF.md under "Deviations from plan", and report it in your final message.
done_when: `src/lib/push.ts` creates Android channel `announcements` (importance high), requests permission, obtains the token with `getExpoPushTokenAsync({ projectId: Constants.expoConfig?.extra?.eas?.projectId })`, validates with `registerPushDeviceSchema` and upserts `push_devices` through `upsertPushDevice`; capability detection returns emulator / expo_go / missing_project_id without throwing.

The Supabase Free project must not be paused (dashboard shows "Active"; restore it if it says paused).
3. Accounts from step 0.1: Expo (expo.dev) and a Google account for Firebase. If deferred, create them now with `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` and turn on two-factor authentication.
4. On your computer: `git pull`, `pnpm install`, `cd apps/mobile`.

**A. EAS project**
5. `npx eas-cli login` → sign in with the Expo account.
6. `npx eas-cli init` → confirm creating the project under your account (slug `anacast`). Because `app.config.ts` is dynamic, EAS prints the project id instead of writing it: copy the `Project ID` (a UUID). Record it in HANDOFF.md → "Mobile (Phase 1)" (it is not a secret) and put it in `apps/mobile/.env` as `EAS_PROJECT_ID=<id>` (the file is gitignored).
7. Confirm with `npx eas-cli project:info` → shows `anacast` and the id.

**B. EAS environment variables (preview environment; repeat later for production)**
8. expo.dev → your project → **Environment variables** → environment **preview** → Add variable, one at a time (or use the `npx eas-cli env:create --environment preview …` commands in MOBILE_BUILD.md §4):
   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` = your Supabase project URL (Supabase → Project Settings → API → Project URL) — plaintext.
   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` = the publishable key (`sb_publishable_…`; or the legacy anon key) — plaintext (it is a public key).
   - `EXPO_PUBLIC_WEB_URL` = `https://<VERCEL_URL>` (the same value as Vercel's `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, no trailing slash) — plaintext.
   - `EAS_PROJECT_ID` = the id from A.6 — plaintext.
   - `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` — type **File**, visibility **Secret** — added in C.11 after you have the file.
9. Also create the same five variables in the **development** environment if you or an agent will run development builds.

**C. Firebase project and Android app**
10. console.firebase.google.com → **Add project** → name `Anacast` → disable Google Analytics → Create. Project settings (gear) → **Your apps** → **Add app** → Android → *Android package name* = exactly the `android.package` value from `apps/mobile/app.config.ts` (print it: `npx expo config --type public | grep '"package"'` — normally `com.anacast.app`; it is immutable after the first Play upload, step 6.5) → nickname `Anacast` → Register app → **Download google-services.json** → skip the remaining SDK steps.
11. Save the downloaded file as `apps/mobile/google-services.json` (gitignored — check with `git status`, it must NOT appear) and upload it to EAS: expo.dev → Environment variables → preview → Add → name `GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON`, type **File**, visibility **Secret**, choose the file → Save (or `npx eas-cli env:create --environment preview --name GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON --type file --value ./google-services.json --visibility secret`). Store a copy in the vault.
12. FCM v1 key: Firebase → Project settings → **Service accounts** → **Generate new private key** → Generate → a JSON file downloads (treat it as a password). Then `npx eas-cli credentials -p android` → select the `preview` build profile (or "All") → **Google Service Account** → **Manage your Google Service Account Key for Push Notifications (FCM V1)** → **Set up a Google Service Account Key** → Upload a new key → pick the downloaded JSON → confirm. Afterwards move the JSON into the vault and delete it from Downloads.

**D. Build and install the preview APK**
13. `npx eas-cli build -p android --profile preview` → answer **Yes** to "Generate a new Android Keystore?" (EAS stores it; you never see it) → wait (10–25 minutes on the free queue). The terminal prints a build page URL.
14. On the phone: open the build page (QR code or link) → **Install** → download the APK → if Android blocks it, allow "Install unknown apps" for your browser → install → open **Anacast**.
15. Record in HANDOFF.md "Mobile (Phase 1)" → builds ledger: `preview | <build id> | <version from app.config.ts> | <date>`.

**E. Checkpoint C — Android trial (tick every line)**
16. Sign-in: enter the email from item 2 → "Email me a code" → a 6-digit code arrives → enter it → the Home tab of your church opens. (If a link arrives instead of a code, fix the template from item 1 and retry.)
17. Notifications: the explainer appears → **Turn on notifications** → Android asks for permission → Allow. Verify on the server: Supabase → SQL Editor → `select platform, enabled, device_name, created_at from public.push_devices;` → one row for your phone.
18. Push from an announcement: on the web (`/o/<slug>/announcements/new`) publish an announcement to **All attendees** with push on → the phone shows a notification within seconds → tap it → the announcement opens in the app. Then repeat with the app fully closed (swipe it away first) → the tap opens the announcement from cold start.
19. Push from a bulletin (founder decision 6, push on by default): upload a bulletin PDF on the web (`/o/<slug>/bulletins`) → notification → tap → the bulletin screen → **Open bulletin** → the phone's PDF viewer shows it.
20. Sermons: play an **uploaded mp3** → lock the phone → audio keeps playing and the lock screen shows the title; play a **YouTube-linked** sermon → it plays inline; open a **Google Drive-linked** sermon → the browser opens (expected, DESIGN §7). If there are no such sermons yet, create them on the web first (`/o/<slug>/sermons/new`, Upload | Link).
21. Notification settings: More → Notification settings → switch **Bulletins** off → upload another bulletin on the web → no push arrives; switch it back on.
22. Session: kill the app and reopen → still signed in. More → Sign out → SQL Editor: the `push_devices` row is gone. Sign in again (the explainer does not reappear if permission is already granted; the row comes back).
23. Optional: a second family member's phone with a second invited account — both receive the same announcement.

**F. Record**
24. HANDOFF.md → "Mobile (Phase 1)": tick the Checkpoint C items, note the EAS project id, build id, version, date, phone model + Android version, and every failure verbatim (screenshots' text, `npx eas-cli build:view` errors). Also add under "Environment status" that the EAS `preview` environment is configured. Commit and push (or hand the notes to the helper prompt below).

**Done when**: an APK built by EAS from `main` is installed on your phone; you signed in with a 6-digit code; `push_devices` shows your phone; an announcement and a bulletin published on the web produced notifications that opened the right screens (including from a cold start); an uploaded sermon played in the background and a YouTube-linked sermon played inline; a bulletin PDF opened; sign-out removed the device row; HANDOFF.md holds the build ledger and the Checkpoint C results.
